title: Seesaw: High-throughput LLM Inference via Model Re-sharding
problem: A single static parallelization strategy (tensor parallelism or pipeline parallelism) cannot optimally serve both the prefill and decode stages of LLM inference, leaving throughput on the table.
motivation: Prefill is compute-bound and benefits from tensor parallelism (TP) across few devices to minimize latency, while decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and benefits from pipeline parallelism (PP) to enable large batch sizes. Existing engines (e.g., vLLM) fix one strategy, causing either prefill or decode to run suboptimally.
method: Seesaw switches the model's parallelization strategy during inference based on the current phase: using tensor parallelism (splitting layers across GPUs) for prefill (processing prompts) and pipeline parallelism (distributing layers sequentially across GPUs) for decode (generating tokens). To manage memory efficiently, the key-value cache—intermediate results needed for fast computation—is stored in fast GPU VRAM for active batches and slower CPU DRAM as overflow storage, with asynchronous background transfers between them. A scheduler batches requests together to reduce how often resharding occurs, spreading the switching cost across multiple requests.
key_novelty: The core idea is dynamically resharding the model between different parallelization strategies mid-inference, combined with tiered KV cache management and request batching to minimize resharding overhead.
contributions: Dynamic model re-sharding framework switching between TP (prefill) and PP (decode) at stage boundaries
Tiered KV cache buffering using CPU DRAM as auxiliary store with async pipeline for swap
Transition-minimizing scheduling policy that batches requests to reduce re-sharding events
End-to-end throughput evaluation showing 1.36x average and 1.78x peak improvement over vLLM
hardware_target: NVIDIA A10, L4, A100 GPUs; multi-GPU server nodes
workloads: Throughput-oriented serving with mixed request batches
limitations: Re-sharding introduces latency spikes at stage boundaries that must be hidden by batching
CPU memory tiering adds host-device PCIe bandwidth pressure
Evaluated only on throughput-oriented workloads; latency-sensitive use cases may differ
